source.title: Withdrawal assessment report for Lenalidomide Celgene Europe
source.extraction: AI-assisted from the PDF text layer; each quote checked against the extracted text. Independent review pending.

study.design: single 25 mg oral dose, fasting; renal function groups by measured creatinine clearance

plasma_protein_binding.method: in vitro ultrafiltration, 30-10000 ng/mL, no concentration dependence
plasma_protein_binding.quote: The mean binding was 23 and 29% in plasma from myeloma patients and healthy volunteers, respectively.

urinary_recovery_unchanged_percent.quote: the overall urinary recovery of unchanged drug being approximately 85% of the administered single oral dose

renal_clearance.quote: Renal clearance was at least 190 ml/min, suggesting that active renal secretion occurs.

secretion_transporters.quote: In vitro studies investigating which transporters are involved in the active renal secretion of lenalidomide are ongoing.

physiology.metabolism: Not metabolised via cytochrome P450; other enzymatic systems not studied (page 20).

group_value_locations.fe: page 21, text below Table 4 (means only; no SD reported)

group_quotes.fe: Subjects with normal renal function had higher mean % dose excreted unchanged in urine (85%), followed by subjects with mild RI (69%), subjects with moderate RI (42%) and subjects with severe RI (44%).

notes: The severe-group CL/F SD of 101 mL/min is printed as such; it may be a typographical error but is transcribed as printed and not used.
End-stage renal disease groups (with and without dialysis) are not transcribed here.
Oral bioavailability is not known (no IV data); 85% urinary recovery of unchanged drug implies F is at least about 0.85.
